purpose: Qualitative allocation diagnosis of separately captured Windows EventPipe traces. No product workload, benchmark or profiler is executed by this analysis.

method.conversion: TraceLog.CreateFromEventPipeDataFile using KeepAllEvents=true, LocalSymbolsOnly=true, ContinueOnError=false; preserved ETLX and conversion logs.
method.reading: TraceLog.Events.GetSource().Clr.GCAllocationTick; GetCallStackForEvent; allocation leaf to root. Payloads are copied before the reused TraceEvent advances.
method.markerEvidence: Generated lambda names observed in rundown stacks. The source marker's stacks include ItemsSource/reset paths and the scroll marker's stacks include ScrollIntoView. Numeric closure IDs alone are not source-line mapping.
method.phasePolicy: Categories describe visible stack structure, not measured/setup phase. In the immutable harness Pump(window) occurs both initially and inside the operation delegate. A missing operation-lambda frame can result from inlining/tailcalls, and no source-line/native-offset mapping is applied here.
method.rawCategoryWarning: Raw parser category is a broad MatchedWorkload lambda heuristic and also includes b__0_0 item creation. Final summary categories use the exact scenario-specific operation lambda above.
method.byteSemantics: GCAllocationTick is emitted after approximately 100 KB of allocation. TypeName and stack describe the threshold-crossing object, not every object or type in the interval. ObjectSize is that trigger object's size. Neither interval sums nor trigger-object sums measure retained memory.
method.lossSemantics: EventsLost and truncation report transport/conversion loss. Zero lost events does not make sampling exhaustive.
method.timingPolicy: Profiled elapsed values are excluded from comparisons and primary timing conclusions.

limitations: Only one separately profiled Windows process exists per source/scenario; profiles are not primary A/B timing measurements.
The same operation lambda is used for warmups and measured invocations; no exact per-iteration markers are present in these profiles.
Whole-process profiles include discovery, setup, window show/close, pumping and teardown. Async work after the operation returns cannot be unambiguously assigned to a synchronous operation stack.
Only 25 baseline and 19 final scroll ticks have an explicit operation-lambda frame. Pump has another 455/476 ticks with phase unresolved, so 25/19 is not the complete operation allocation count.
Sampling cannot attribute a precise 578-byte difference or establish retained memory, and cannot confirm or refute the separate Linux scroll timing estimates.

Method names resolve from runtime rundown. A small number of samples have some unresolved frames, even though every tick has a stack with named frames. No external native symbol resolution was requested.
